  Mayor Huff presented a Proclamation supporting Energy Upgrade California’s “Do Your

B.  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  PROCLAIMING APRIL 24, 2018 AS A “DAY OF REMEMBRANCE” OF THE ARMENIAN
  GENOCIDE OF 1915-1923

  Mayor Huff proclaimed April 24, 2018 as a “Day of Remembrance” of the Armenian
  Genocide of 1915-1923.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked Supervisor Janice Hanh for recognizing the
  South Bay Armenian Center in Lomita at today’s Board of Supervisors meeting and
  noted his appreciation to the COUNCIL for their support of this proclamation for the
  last 15 years. He commented that this is a human rights issue and that he will work to
  continue to bring attention to crimes against humanity. He expressed his sadness at
  the atrocities still taking place throughout the world and encouraged everyone to reflect
  on those groups in the past and present who have suffered this kind of bloodshed. He
  relayed a story of endurance and survival of how this tragedy affected his family and
  noted that many other cultures who have suffered similar brutality. He stated that his
  hope is that this crime would be designated as a genocide by the government and
  encouraged everyone to stand up for human rights; and although he cannot bring his
  ancestors back, he would like to prevent the next one from happening by sharing this
  story.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 24 2018
   He then shared a PowerPoint presentation providing a history of the Armenian Genocide
  and highlighting the act of kindness that the Near East Relief Foundation provided
  during this tragedy which involved rescue efforts for the Armenian orphans and was
  supported by several U.S. Presidents and many U.S. citizens. Finally, he asked God to
  bless the soles of our ancestors and give us the courage to stand for what is legally and
  morally right and to demand justice.

  MAYOR HUFF and COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN presented the Proclamation to
  representatives from the South Bay Armenian Center.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
  cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
  consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-G AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  CAPSTONE PROJECT: MULTIJURISDICTIONAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND
  COMMUNICATION STRATEGY

  Students from University of Southern California’s Sol Price School of Public Policy reviewed
  a presentation providing the results of their research regarding Multijurisdictional
  Emergency Preparedness and Communication Strategy specifically focused on the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula and Rolling Hills Estates. The recommendations included: (1) develop a
  communication strategy with an emphasis on the use of social media using the resident
  preparedness campaign, “You don’t need to get ready if you stay ready”; (2) create an
  Emergency Communication Plan; (3) create a Reverse 911 System and communication
  redundancies; and (4) create Public Private Partnerships.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

  NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: 2018 CITY CELEBRATION VENUE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Ernie Howlett park as the venue for
  the City Celebration on September 15, 2018.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Vicki Shinn, 23 Roanwood Drive expressed her appreciation and respect for the City’s
  long-standing equestrian heritage and suggested that the City Celebration be held at
  the Empty Saddle Club to embrace that heritage. She further suggested that the event
  be separate from the music festival. She noted that the event was more successful when
  it was held at the Empty Saddle Club.

  Bill Kemp, 3571 Lariat Lane also expressed his appreciation for City’s equestrian
  heritage and suggested that the City Celebration be moved back to the Empty Saddle
  Club.

  Carrie Silvano, 4709 Rockbluff Drive expressed her appreciation for the City’s
  equestrian heritage and suggested that the City Celebration be moved back to the Empty
  Saddle Club and be separated from the music festival.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 24 2018
   Debbie Taymour, RHE resident addressed the COUNCIL in support of moving the City
  Celebration back to the Empty Saddle Club to more reflect the City’s equestrian heritage.

  Sean Martin. 2 Empty Saddle addressed the COUNCIL in support of moving the City
  Celebration back to the Empty Saddle Club and expressed concern regarding the
  logistical difficulties in holding the City Celebration at Ernie Hewlett Park. He also
  suggested having two separate events.

  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission Chair addressed the COUNCIL to
  explain the Commission’s reasoning for recommending that the event be held at Ernie
  Howlett Park. He noted that much thought was put into the decision making process
  with the Commission attempting to address the situation at a higher level and create an
  event that is inclusive of all of the City’s demographics and interests.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF regarding the concerns expressed by the equestrians
  related to the logistical difficulties in getting to Ernie Howlett Park and the coordination
  of both event, Mr. Romanelli commented that the P&A Commission is committed to
  working on ways to make both events successful.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Mr. Romanelli acknowledged that last
  year’s City Celebration was minimally successful but the P&A Commission and City
  Celebration subcommittee are committed to making it successful this year.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Romanelli commented that the
  Empty Saddle Club is not well suited for hosting the music festival. Community Services
  Director Clark explained how the two events came to be held together.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the events seem to be better suited as
  separate events. He suggested having the equestrian events at the Empty Saddle Club
  and on the same day, having the Music Festival at Ernie Howlett Park.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that the City Celebration should strongly
  embrace the City’s equestrian heritage and suggested holding the events in separate
  locations but on the same day with one in the morning and one in the
  afternoon/evening. City Manager Prichard noted that it should be kept in mind that
  there are also the community booths to consider.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he sees the events at two separate
  events.

  Discussion ensued concerning both events and the pros and cons of holding the events
  together. Further discussion ensued concerning the changing makeup of the community
  and ways to attract a broader base of community members.

  Mike Giglia, Park and Activities Commission Vice Chair commented that the Music
  Festival was not the main focus of the City Celebration it was just a way to get more
  people there. He noted that with a concerted effort to engage other community groups,
  the attendance in general increase the last two years. He further commented that the
  P&A Commission and the City Celebration committee are committed to working on ways
  to make the City Celebration successful.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 24 2018
   COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that it should also be taken into
  consideration that there is more logistical support for the equestrian events if the City
  Celebration is held at the Empty Saddle Club. She further commented that she also
  sees the Music Festival and City Celebration as two separate events.

  Discussion ensued concerning the Music Festival with the COUNCIL expressing its
  support for the event and suggesting that the Park & Activities Commission work with
  the event organizers to facilitate the event.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE EMPTY SADDLE CLUB AS THE VENUE
  FOR THE CITY CELEBRATION ON SEPTEMBER 15, 2018

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITIES
  NAMING POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the attached revised City Property and
  Facilities Naming Policy.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that since the existing policy allows for naming
  a facility after a person who is still living, it should not be changed. MAYOR PRO TEM
  MITCHELL concurred.

  Following discussion, the COUNCIL concurred that the policy should not include a
  preference for naming a facility after a person who is still living.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITIES NAMING
  POLICY AS AMENDED TO ADD AFTER IN PERPETUITY “EXCEPT AS PROVIDED
  FOR IN SECTION 5” AND FOR THE RECOMMENDATION TO COME FROM THE
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  DEVELOPMENT CONSULTANT

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the proposal does not include a site plan
  or electrical plan and that may be something to look into.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
APRIL 24 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Community Services Director Clark
  noted that there will be parking west of the park, on both sides of Palos Verdes Drive
  East but the park will be mostly a walk-to or bike-to park.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ENTERING INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH
  BMLA LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A ¼ ACRE
  PARK ON THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

D.  PROJECT LIST FOR SB-1 FUND ELIGIBILITY

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the specifications and bid documents;
  and authorize solicitation of bids for the 2018-19 Resurfacing Project on Various Streets.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ noted that the PVPUSD school-year calendar may be

  project.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE SPECIFICATIONS AND BID
  DOCUMENTS; AND AUTHORIZE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE 2018-19
  RESURFACING PROJECT ON VARIOUS STREETS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
APRIL 24 2018
 F.  MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT – TORRANCE AIRPORT STORM WATER
  INFILTRATION PROJECT STAKEHOLDER GROUP – PRELIMINARY DESIGN WORK
  COST SHARING AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the Memorandum
  of Agreement for the Torrance Airport Storm Water Infiltration Project Stakeholder
  Group for Preliminary Design Cost Sharing Agreement, subject to final review and
  approval by the City Attorney.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting commented that this is a worthy project that
  could potentially address the water quality requirements for most of the area of the City.
  Additionally, the project could potentially provide water supply benefits which could
  potentially lead to outside funding. Ms. McGowan further explained the two possible
  paths that the project could take depending on the results of the preliminary design
  work.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, Ms. McGowan explained the cost sharing
  matrix based on the modified scope of work.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Ms. McGowan explained that this
  agreement is for the preliminary design work and if it is deemed feasible, the City would
  then be responsible of its portion of the final design work.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE
  MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT FOR THE TORRANCE AIRPORT STORM
  WATER INFILTRATION PROJECT STAKEHOLDER GROUP – PRELIMINARY
  DESIGN COST SHARING AGREEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $66,477.00,
